tldr: Q3 GDP smashed consensus at 3.4% annualized (vs 3.2% expected) with core PCE sticky at 3.1% y/y -- a 'no landing' print that validates Wednesday's hawkish 10-2 Fed dissent and pushed December-hike odds to ~85%, pressuring gold (-0.38% to ~$4,036) and silver (-2.49% to ~$52.13) further into the open.

BOJ held at 1.25% this morning but 83% of economists now expect a December hike, up from 35% a month ago -- a second hawkish G3 central bank, adding a yen-strength variable on top of the Fed story for HK tech and Asia risk sentiment.

HK Southbound selling re-accelerated to a 12th straight day (~HK$33.8bn cumulative) after briefly decelerating Wednesday -- SMIC (0981) was the largest single-name net-sell two sessions running, a genuine headwind for the HK-tech sleeve.

China's rare-earth export-control truce stays genuinely unresolved 11 days from the Nov 10 deadline: Washington claims a broader extension to Jan 2027 but Beijing has published no matching legal text -- the single biggest near-term catalyst for the MP/Lynas/rare-earth watchlist.
Credit is quality-selective: broad high-yield spreads look calm (~3.2-3.4% OAS) but CCC-and-lower sits at a record-wide ~13.1% -- an early-warning signal worth tracking, not yet systemic.

Three different congressional sellers unloaded Microsoft right before Thursday's beat (Azure +48%), while Oracle's Investor Day (+11%) convinced the Street AI capex pays off on the same day Alphabet's cash-flow miss couldn't.
